themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions complaints spiked to 205 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 35.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 478% surge (z-score: 7.21)—suggesting rapid deterioration of road quality across Sunnyside/Woodside, potentially linked to winter weather or deferred maintenance.
evidence: 205 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 35.5-complaint weekly average over prior 8 weeks (478% increase, z-score 7.21)
Street Sweeping Complaint also up 1500% (6 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 baseline) suggesting systemic street maintenance failure
Street Condition is already #3 category by volume over 90 days (1,121 complaints), now accelerating sharply
reporting_angles: Field reporting: photograph worst-affected blocks; identify potholes, flooding, or structural damage triggering surge
Interview Department of Transportation on repair backlog and timeline; ask if winter weather or budget constraints are drivers

themes_detail.label: Homeless Encampments Expanding
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 23 THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 5.2 per week—a 338% spike (z-score: 5.94)—indicating a sudden increase in visible homelessness across the district.
evidence: 23 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.2-complaint weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (338% increase, z-score 5.94)
Aligns with broader NYC homelessness crisis; Sunnyside/Woodside showing acute localized acceleration
Community board budget requests include park improvements—suggests residents want more public space investment, possibly exacerbated by encampment visibility
reporting_angles: Interview DHS and NYPD on whether they've deployed additional outreach teams to district; ask about shelter capacity
Speak with affected residents in high-encampment areas (likely near parks or transit hubs); assess public safety and sanitation concerns

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints skyrocketed to 5 three weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 3900% spike (z-score: 14.74, highest severity)—indicating widespread graffiti, posters, or unauthorized signage blanketing the district.
evidence: 5 illegal posting complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1-complaint weekly baseline (3900% increase, z-score 14.74—highest severity in dataset)
Suggests coordinated campaign (political posters, promotions, vandalism) or infrastructure neglect enabling widespread posting
Street Sweeping Complaint also elevated (1500% spike), suggesting broader sanitation system failure
reporting_angles: Visual audit: photograph affected streets and document types of posters (political, commercial, vandalism); map concentration areas
Interview Parks/Sanitation on enforcement frequency and whether posting complaints have dropped in past 2 weeks (trend reversal?)

themes_detail.label: Vaping & Smoking Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Smoking or Vaping complaints jumped to 15 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 3.5 per week—a 329% increase (z-score: 6.93)—suggesting either increased enforcement of indoor smoking bans or a genuine uptick in public vaping/smoking violations.
evidence: 15 smoking/vaping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.5-complaint weekly baseline (329% increase, z-score 6.93)
May reflect shift in resident enforcement behavior (more complaints filed) or genuine behavioral change (increased vaping in public spaces)
Public health angle: youth vaping trends may be concentrated in transit-rich neighborhoods like Sunnyside
reporting_angles: Verify with NYPD/DOH whether enforcement campaign or education initiative was launched in past 2-3 weeks
Interview school officials or youth programs about vaping prevalence; check if spike correlates with youth activity patterns

themes_detail.label: Building Safety Issues Emerging
themes_detail.summary: BEST (Building Exterior & Site Threats) Safety complaints spiked to 3 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—plus Building/Use violations up 380% two weeks ago, suggesting facade failures, structural hazards, or code violations clustering in the district.
evidence: BEST/Site Safety complaints: 3 LAST WEEK vs. 0.1-complaint weekly baseline (2300% increase, z-score 8.69)
Building/Use violations: 12 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.5-complaint baseline (380% increase, z-score 5.27)
640 building permits filed in last 90 days (109 new buildings, 431 alterations); possible link to construction-related hazards or code violations
reporting_angles: Cross-reference DOB violation database: identify which blocks or building types are generating BEST complaints; check if any address patterns emerge
Interview DOB on recent enforcement surge or hazard sweep; determine if complaints signal aging building stock, recent construction accidents, or facade maintenance backlog
